An original naval marksman on the RIGHT half of a wooden ship deck, three-quarter standing view, dark navy coat, brass trim, leather boots, warm lantern and blue sea. He holds ONE compact historically plausible flintlock carbine in a relaxed low-ready pose across his waist. Weapon length about the distance from his hip to opposite shoulder, NOT taller than his body. One straight narrow steel barrel, one continuous wooden stock with distinct broad shoulder butt, one trigger and brass trigger guard. Right hand grips the stock wrist immediately behind the trigger; left hand supports the wooden fore-end beneath the barrel. Muzzle directed diagonally down-left, buttstock beside right upper arm. Clear functional firearm silhouette, consistent straight barrel, no crossed poles, no duplicated barrels, no second weapon, no extensions beyond muzzle or butt. Anatomically coherent hands and five fingers, no fused hands. Keep entire carbine and both hands inside canvas. Left quarter quiet dark rigging to blend into interface.
